newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends higher, profit-taking saps strength.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends higher, profit-taking saps strength.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended higher Tuesday, but profit-taking and farmer selling limited advances, pit traders said.
"We saw a lot of profit-taking and a lot of farmer hedging," said one pit trader. "The farmers are loving these prices."
Some trading Tuesday was linked to position squaring ahead of the U.S. Agriculture Department's crop report on Friday and export sales data on Thursday, traders said.
Support in the market was tied to talk that Iraq had purchased large quantities of inexpensive rice from Thailand, Taiwan, Vietnam and Pakistan, traders said.
Both March and July made fresh contract highs Tuesday.
Commercials were buying January, and funds were noted rolling out of January and buying March and May, pit sources said.
Rice volume was estimated 500 contracts, down from 741 on Monday, according to CBOT data.
Rice closed 0.01 to 0.03 cents per cwt higher, with January up 0.03 at $11.13 and March up 0.01 cent at $11.22.
